decisions.reason: The reference paragraph conflates projection measurability with integral monotonicity. Measurability follows directly because the inverse image of B is the measurable rectangle S×B; integral monotonicity then bounds the reward mean by K(S×[0,1])=1. The Definition is unchanged.

For q=0 and a positive-reward unknown action, the prescribed sink value 0 is pessimistic. The general Definition correctly prescribes capped absorbing values and claims no optimism; corrected the misleading title and its manifest mirror without restricting q or changing the Definition.

Step 1.1 incorrectly says every failed batch disables learning. Replaced its load-bearing batch-count argument by an injection from consecutive batch-start intervals into successful global updates; the disjoint intervals give the required N bound, including unfinished batches. Also made AC explicit for the actual concentration prerequisite and defined S,A. The optimism and 2mG proofs retain their claims.

A1 overattributes path-law existence to the choice-function axiom. Corrected A1 to state AC and its use as a hypothesis; F2 now explicitly attributes trajectory laws to the already-cited value-functions theorem. Both suppliers were already dependencies and AC was already in the Statement. The stopped coupling, C=B+W cap, disjoint trials and exponential estimate remain valid.

F4 incorrectly describes finite-sum laws as sums distributing over products. Replaced it by the actual additivity, scaling and monotonicity clauses and displayed sum_c w(h)p(c|h)=w(h), with induction normalizing the finite tree and verifying its marginals in step 2.1. The two-bandit contradiction and legal R-MAX/delayed-Q witnesses remain sound. Added the explicit AC dependency already assumed in the unchanged Statement.

The Example already identifies inadmissibility but does not explicitly define its domain extension of alg-r-max. Specified that only U≥Q* is dropped and all procedure instructions remain unchanged; F1 now cites those retained instructions. Direct induction at gamma=0 keeps both values zero after the one-sweep rebuild, so the tie rule chooses b forever. This claims no application of the admissible-input guarantee.

The original Statement omits AC required by the escape reduction, zero-tolerance theorem, value theorem and concentration lemma. Added the explicit assumption and dependency. Also closed the digest concern in step 1.3 by extending V_t to each dedicated sink with value Q_t(s,a), giving zero sink residual and a valid maximum over the whole model. Checked all parameter substitutions, confidence delta/2 and barred uniform bounds.
